evidence.location: §0 'Same verdict as GND'; Goal and completion predicates, RP1
evidence.observation: §0 states: "On every input a program accepts, it reports a rule as not checked exactly where `gnd check` (without an anchor sidecar) does. A program that enforces less than GND checks is a defect; one that enforces more is a defect too." The RP1 predicate states: "A disconnected join is reported as GND reports it: vacuous when every referenced fact list is empty, otherwise not checked with GND's reason". Neither carries a per-target carve-out for LQP.

RP1-C6 requires "(oracle) a disconnected external join agrees with GND on a population with facts (not checked, exit 4) and on one with every referenced list empty (vacuous, exit 2)". A2 amends only "§1 and RP1-C6, disconnected join 'vacuous when its lists are empty'" and adds "The DuckDB version reads the computed view of semiderived types; the LQP version always lists it as not checked"; no §11 row amends §0 or the RP1 goal predicate.

evidence.location: Boundaries, third bullet; Goal predicates table, RP1 row
evidence.observation: Boundaries records: "The LQP version lists a disconnected join as not checked even when GND calls it vacuous (exit 4 where GND gives 2)." The Goal predicates table nevertheless reads "RP1: external uniqueness in `--rules duckdb|lqp` ... | holds | `003-phase-RP1.md`: C1–C9; agreement on raw (0), duplicate (1), empty join (2), disconnected (4/4/2), renamed, numeric, three-way", where the notation "4/4/2" gives no per-target reading of the divergence.

concerns.recommendation: Either restore vacuity (exit 2) in the LQP program for a disconnected join whose referenced lists are all empty, or add a §11 amendment that narrows §0's 'Same verdict as GND' rule and the RP1 predicate/RP1-C6 to the DuckDB target, names the LQP exit-4-where-GND-exits-2 case as a stated difference on docs/runtimes/pyrel.md, and then restates the RP1 row of close-results against the amended predicate instead of the unamended one.
concerns.title: LQP disconnected-join verdict (exit 4 where GND exits 2) contradicts §0 and the unamended RP1 predicate, yet RP1 is recorded as holding

evidence.observation: §3 requires: "A phase that makes a shape newly lowerable (RP1's external uniqueness and `String` entity, RP3's `Number`, RP4's role-scoped and fact-scoped value) adds a test that `gnd export ossie` on a model with that shape gives the bytes it gave at `8c909013`, because the committed Ossie tests cover none of them." No criterion in §4 (RP1-C1..C9, RP3-C1..C5, RP4-C1..C3) names such a test.
A5 records "holds; RP4 needed one Ossie line to keep it (fact-scoped value rules stay extensions)", i.e. `src/gnd/export/ossie_formulas.py` was edited during the milestone to preserve its output.

evidence.location: Goal predicates table, RP4 row; Last gates
evidence.observation: The RP4 evidence is "`005-phase-RP4.md`: C1–C3; 573 accepted programs byte-identical", which counts rules programs, not Ossie output; no line of close-results names an Ossie byte-pin test for RP1's external uniqueness/`String` entity, RP3's `Number`, or RP4's role- and fact-scoped value shapes.

concerns.recommendation: Name the Ossie pin tests (file and test id) in close-results for each newly lowerable shape, or add a §11 row stating why §3's pin requirement was dropped and what now guards the edited Ossie line against regression.
concerns.title: §3's required Ossie byte-pin tests for the newly lowerable shapes are not evidenced, although an Ossie source line was edited to keep the bytes

evidence.observation: The header asserts "The canonical statement of each is plan §11", and item 8 states "**Comparator** (RP3). The shared comparator compares witness numbers by GND's identity (`1` = `1.0`), because the programs print Float values as floats." Plan §11 contains rows A1-A7 only (joins, refusals, D6 bound, Ossie, generated names, runtime page); none covers the comparator.

evidence.location: Goal and completion predicates, final paragraph; §4 RP2-C6
evidence.observation: The plan makes the comparator the instrument of every agreement claim: "RP2 extends both sides to `(rule, 'not checked', null)`, with a negative control (RP2-C6), before any criterion relies on it", and RP2-C6's control is only "the negative control (one anchored id dropped from `UNCHECKED`) fails it"; no control is named for witness-number equality, which RP3 relaxed.

Every predicate row rests on oracle agreement ("twelve gold populations agree", "56 populations agree") and the oracle lane is reported only as an aggregate ("338 passed, 151 deselected"), with no statement of which agreement results were re-run after the comparator's identity change in RP3.

concerns.recommendation: Add a §11 row (or a close-delta pointer to the RP3 record) stating the comparator change, name a negative control that fails when two witnesses differ beyond GND's numeric identity, and record in close-results which agreement tests were re-run after the change landed.
concerns.title: The oracle comparator's witness-equality semantics were relaxed in RP3 with no §11 amendment and no named negative control, though all 'agrees with GND' evidence depends on it

evidence.observation: The section records "RP3: 5 rounds, plus 2 attempts with no verdict (provider flag). The last repair has no second reader." and "RP5: 3 rounds, stopped by the convergence rule. The last sentence has no second reader."

§8 requires for "Each phase: spec, delegated spec gate, code, focused gates, one independent reviewer over the diff (the review helper with Codex, read-only; one reviewer is one reviewer), refactoring review, record, commit", so shipped bytes produced after the reviewer's last verdict are outside the recorded protocol.

Boundaries lists only the engine, the D4/D6/A4 strictness, the LQP disconnected listing and the no-sidecar scope; it does not carry the two unreviewed final edits, and no §11 row records the deviation from §8.

concerns.recommendation: Before the close gate is recorded, obtain one independent read of RP3's last repair diff and of the RP5 sentence, or move both disclosures into close-results' Boundaries with the reason they are accepted and a §11 row noting the departure from §8.
concerns.title: RP3's last repair and RP5's last sentence shipped after the independent reviewer's final verdict and are not carried as a boundary

evidence.observation: The plan's final verification row reads "| all | the structure and inventory guard block of `project.md`, and `uv run ruff check` | — | exit 0 |", i.e. the unscoped command at exit 0.

close-results reports "`uv run ruff check src tests tools`: clean. Whole-tree `ruff check`: 198 errors, the known red in dev-tools-delivered skill scripts, unchanged since the base." The clean result is a narrower path set than §9's command, and "unchanged since the base" cites no baseline measurement in any of the three artifacts.

concerns.recommendation: Record the whole-tree ruff count measured at the base (`8c909013`) beside the 198 figure, or add a §11 row narrowing §9's ruff gate to `src tests tools` with the reason, so the gate the plan states and the gate that was run are the same gate.
concerns.title: The reported ruff gate is narrower than §9's whole-tree 'exit 0' requirement, and the 198 residual errors have no cited baseline

evidence.observation: RP5-C1 reads "these eleven packaged models render under both targets, exit 0: `model.orm.yaml`, `assertions/model.orm.yaml`, `lineage/model.orm.yaml`, `resolution/model.orm.yaml`, `quantity_fixture/time.orm.yaml`, `interop_fixture/extraction.orm.json`, `interop_fixture/checking.orm.json`, and `depth_fixture/{algorithms,decimal,dynamics,molecular,vocabulary}.orm.json`" — seven named paths plus a five-member brace expansion, i.e. twelve models, not eleven.

evidence.location: Goal and completion predicates, RP5; §1 subsection headings
evidence.observation: The RP5 predicate reads "Every packaged literature model in §1's acceptance table exports under both `--rules duckdb` and `--rules lqp`, exit 0", but §1's subsections are "Observed refusals", "Populations for the agreement criteria", "What GND itself does with each construct (measured)", "Sources" and "Issue requests and the phases that discharge them"; there is no acceptance table, and the refusals table holds nine rows including "#214's six-line `Number` model", which RP5-C1 excludes.
close-results records "`006-phase-RP5.md`: 12 models × 2 targets", a third figure for the same acceptance set.

concerns.recommendation: Correct "eleven" to the twelve paths RP5-C1 enumerates and repoint the RP5 goal predicate at §4's RP5-C1 list (or name the §1 table it means), so the set the close measured is the set the plan states.
concerns.title: RP5's acceptance set is given as eleven models but enumerates twelve, its predicate cites a §1 'acceptance table' that does not exist, and close-results reports 12

evidence.observation: §11 states "Each names the record that raised it; the r4 wording above is kept as written" under the column heading "Section, prior wording kept", but A2 anchors to "§1 and RP1-C6, disconnected join 'vacuous when its lists are empty'" — a phrase that occurs in neither place in r4 (§1 reads "vacuous, exit 2, when both referenced fact lists are empty, and **unchecked**, exit 4, otherwise"; RP1-C6 reads "on one with every referenced list empty (vacuous, exit 2)") — and A3 anchors to "§0 'Same verdict on accepted inputs'", while §0's rule is headed "**Same verdict as GND.**"

concerns.recommendation: Re-anchor A2 and A3 to the r4 sentences they actually narrow, quoting them verbatim, so a reader can diff each amendment against the kept wording as §11 promises.
concerns.title: §11 amendments A2 and A3 quote prior wording that does not occur in the r4 sections they name, breaking the table's 'prior wording kept' contract

summary: Traced the five goal predicates to their criteria and gate numbers: §4's criterion counts match close-results (RP1 C1-C9, RP2 C1-C8, RP3 C1-C5, RP4 C1-C3), the 56 agreeing populations equal §1's table (12 gold + 1 assertions + 41 resolution + 1 quantity + 1 decimal), all five §10 open questions are dispositioned in §11's sweep, and D1-D6 are all decided. One blocking concern: the LQP program's not-checked listing of a disconnected join contradicts §0's 'Same verdict as GND' rule, the RP1 goal predicate and RP1-C6's '(vacuous, exit 2)', while §11 A2 amends only §1 and RP1-C6's vacuity wording and close-results still records RP1 'holds'. Hardening: the §3 Ossie byte-pin tests for the newly lowerable shapes are named nowhere even though A5 records an edited Ossie line; the comparator's witness-identity change (close-delta 8) carries no §11 row and no negative control although every oracle agreement claim rests on it; RP3's last repair and RP5's last sentence have no second reader against §8; and the ruff gate was narrowed from whole-tree exit 0 to 'src tests tools' with 198 residual errors asserted pre-existing without a cited baseline. Completeness: RP5's acceptance set is stated as 'eleven' but enumerates twelve and its predicate cites a '§1 acceptance table' that §1 does not contain, and A2/A3 quote prior wording that does not occur in the r4 sections they name.
